comment: He cares about all his students and takes the time to get to know them. There are a bunch of writing assignments, but they aren't terrible. Make sure you participate in class. Grading can be unclear at times for writing, but it is fair. Do your best

221 is not as bad as it seems and I would strongly recommend to take him if he is teaching it. He's incredibly thorough, really cares for his students inside and outside of class, easily accessible and genuinely wants you to do well. If you want to do well and actually learn the language, then he is for you. Best teacher I've had so far.

Prof. G's classes are engaging, especially his upper-level seminar with minimal research paper readings. Understanding isn't crucial as topics are discussed in class. Participation requires completing readings. Grading is fair and lenient.

I took Dr. G for his FYS spring semester--not his Spanish class (this was not an option yet when choosing his class).  Some classes of FYS were more interesting than others though and the writing topics could be tough. Still, he is great, really into his topic and provides great writing feedback and is very open to helping students which is awesome

Professor Giancaspro is very knowledgeable and funny. He cares for his students and ensures that you are getting along well in his class. If you put the work in, your Spanish will get much better under his watch. He doesn't give a lot of homework, so be prepared to study for his quizzes and tests.

Prof. Giancaspro is great. This was one of my favorite classes of the semester. You got to read a lot though. There were a couple of writing assignments, but they were not long or hard to write about. He's not picky when it comes to grading.

He's very understanding of his students. If you have a chance to take him, do it.

Prof. G is a good professor. He did a really good job with the course. For me, I wish that he would have spoken more English. There were times when I was confused and did not understand a concept, but did not know how to ask it in Spanish. All in all, LAIS 151 just is not a great class. It meets 5 days a week, but Prof G made it bearable.

VHL website homework three times a week, probably about 30 to do each HW, but quizlet has answers if. He speaks spanish most of the class. He goes over vocab+grammar examples but if you're not familiar then study. clear outlines for tests. 3 noncumulative tests(no midterm) and the final. multiple short quizzes. Easy A if you know spanish. Nice guy

Professor Giancaspro is absolutely amazing, he enjoys speaking with his students in and out of class and gives good feedback. He is willing to help if you reach out to him. He does enjoy discussions and likes for all of his students to participate.
Professor Giancaspro needs a reality check. His class is unnecessarily difficult. He gives way too many assignments and thinks way too highly of himself. Worst class I took in college.
Great professor for 221. If you participate you will do well.

Really kind guy who facilitates discussion well and gets his students involved. He expects you to be prepared and serious about the course. Loves to talk to his students before and after class, he is really accessible. Tough grader on essays and there are a lot of tests and quizzes but all in all very fair and I liked him a lot

Professor Giancaspro has a good classroom atmosphere, but the work outside of class is extreme. He is strict. 5-6 papers. No room for error on the papers. Tough grading. Hard for non-native speaker to succeed in class and receive an A. Be ready to participate.
